name: rs485_thvd1410
title: RS-485 transceiver
purpose: Half-duplex RS-485 link to the flight computer on the Pi's UART (THVD1410, 500 kbps)

sources.title: TI THVD1410/THVD1450 3.3-V to 5-V RS-485 transceivers (SLLSEY3E)
sources.licence: TI datasheet; link and quotes only
sources.read: p1, p5 pin functions, p8-9 ratings, p18-22 description and termination, p28-29 supply and layout

parts.quote: D package (SOIC) pins: R 1, RE 2, DE 3, D 4, GND 5, A 6, B 7, VCC 8 (Pin Functions); "VCC Supply voltage 3 … 5.5 V"; "two speed grades suitable for data transmission up to 500 kbps and 50 Mbps" (THVD1410: 500 kbps). Symbol: KiCad's THVD1450D, the same pins
"each supply should be decoupled with a 100 nF ceramic capacitor located as close to the supply pins as possible"
"each cable end is terminated with a termination resistor, RT, whose value matches the characteristic impedance, Z0"

/RS485_DIR.note: DE and RE together: high transmits, low receives (DE "active high", RE "active low", p5)

layout.rules: thvd p29: decoupling "100-nF to 220-nF" close to VCC. A and B short and side by side to the connector.

open_questions: RT1's value is the cable's characteristic impedance (not chosen yet); fit it only if this end of the bus is a cable end.
No external failsafe biasing needed: "The receiver output remains logic high under a bus-idle or bus-short conditions without the need for external failsafe biasing resistors" (p19).
The THVD1410 is chosen over the THVD1450 for its 500 kbps speed grade; KiCad has no THVD1410 symbol, the THVD1450D's pins are the same (p5).
